newsitem.title: USA: Calif. agriculture damage estimated at $245 mln.
newsitem.headline: Calif. agriculture damage estimated at $245 mln.

text.p: Recent storms and flooding in California caused an estimated $245 million in damage to agriculture, the state said on Wednesday.
The figure, released by the California Department of Food and Agriculture, was up from initial estimates of $155 million released earlier this month.
The department said the new total included $124 million in damage to infrastructure, private levees, farm equipment, buildings and irrigation systems.
The department said 59,000 acres of crops had been lost, with an additional 95,000 acres damaged by the rain and flooding, for an estimated loss of $89 million total.
Among the commodities worst hit were winegrapes, alfalfa, wheat and broccoli, the department said.
Winegrape losses were estimated at $13.9 million, alfalfa at $15.2 million, wheat and barley at $8.1 million and broccoli at $3.4 million.
The department said walnut losses were estimated at $16.9 million, while plum and prune losses were put at $6.1 million and almond losses at $3.7 million.
Livestock and dairy losses, including losses in milk production, dead animals and destroyed feed, were estimated at about $16.4 million, the department said.
State Agriculture Secretary Ann Veneman released the new figures to the state Senate Budget and Fiscal Review Committee, meeting in Sacramento.
"It will be months before we know the overall impact of these floods because many crops are currently dormant and some areas are still flooded," she said.
The New Year's floods damaged thousands of homes and inundated wide areas of farmland, causing at least $1.5 billion of damage in California, state officials estimated.
